nativeness.why: Three readers, and the third the mildest: 29 observations, none serious, the not-found block and the language bar read cleanly, and the functional layer passed whole («مینو», «اشتراک کریں», «لنک کاپی ہو گیا ✓», «رہائش», «سیر کریں», the colon of list.lead). Two wordings of this round, «زرعی فارم» and the 'check' form of map.locate.err, are built of read parts and unread as wholes.

compliance.why: The independent proof passed the round-2 text on all eleven items: no forbidden letterform and no non-Latin digit in 5031 code points, every name byte-identical («الاحساء» 16 times), every loan equal to an entry that cites P16, the agreements at the seams of the edits right; the stage checker reports nothing. The record that binds the next batches is complete: N4 and its string agree again, and the garment has its entry («چوغہ», with «چوغے» and «چوغوں»). One point off: five entries stay pending («حسی», «مفلق», «بندرگاہ», «حساوی لیموں کا باغ», «براؤزر»), three genders follow usage against a printed label («بندرگاہ», «ریت», «کھجوریں»), and this round's three strings await their proof.

fit.why: Down one, though the text is better than in round 2: the third reader made two things unanimous that had been charged lightly. For: the palms in lakh («25 لاکھ+»), the menu, the share verb and the copied-link message passed every reader who saw them; the location message now says what the source says in a clause the third reader found clear; the header was verified on a real build. Against, two points: «حسی», the word the name section is about, was misread by all three readers on three wordings and stays unpronounceable to them (N7, open); «داستانوں» beside early Islam rang of legend to all three (home.route.s4.d); all three look for a noun the message may not use («لوکیشن»); and the site's own name stands only in Latin, with «UR» on the button.

calibration.question: Large numbers: the source's scale («ملین») or the Urdu scale («لاکھ», «کروڑ»)? And the form of the big figure on the home page.
candidates: A — digits and scale as the source: «2.5 ملین سے زیادہ»
B — the Urdu scale: «25 لاکھ سے زیادہ»; on the figure card in words or compact («25 لاکھ+»)
C — the Urdu scale in words: «پچیس لاکھ سے زیادہ»
calibration.evidence: USAGE. The reader stopped and converted, and wrote «25 لاکھ سے زیادہ» (observation 14): 'I count in lakh and crore; ملین is fine for dollars in a news bulletin, not for counting trees'. His own paper on this very figure: «الاحسا میں 25 لاکھ سے زیادہ کھجوروں کے درخت ہیں» (2020), «20 لاکھ کے قریب» (2025), «ڈھائی لاکھ» beside «33 ملین» for the national figure — lakh three times out of three for these palms. Reference: the ur.wikipedia article «ملین» defines it as 'a numeral unit of the English language, equal to دس لاکھ' and the article «لاکھ» as the unit used in Pakistan; in counts of things both are alive («لاکھ افراد» 262 pages against «ملین افراد» 217; «لاکھ سے زائد» 188 against 125). Dictionary: Rekhta heads «لاکھ — اسم، مذکر، عددی — سوہزار» and gives 'million' as «دس لاکھ»; its only headword spelled «ملین» is another word (soft, laxative; so too Platts), the numeral being a headword of Urdu Lughat alone, defined as «دس لاکھ». Precedent: the Chinese line converts to its own scale with other digits («250 多万»). LAYOUT, measured in place on the build (a fact about form, not about scale): in words the figure breaks onto two lines from 768px up in either scale («25 لاکھ سے زیادہ» 168.2px in a 256px card at 1280); compact it stands on one line at every width («25 لاکھ+» 126.3px), level with the three figures beside it. Round 2: the second reader, a fresh one, read «25 لاکھ سے زیادہ» in the lead and «25 لاکھ+» on the figure card and had no remark on either; the independent proof checked the conversion (2.5 × 10 lakh = 25 lakh) and the form of the figure code point by code point. Round 3: the third reader read both strings without remark. Passed by both readers who saw the lakh figure.
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: B. Counts in /ur/ text are written in the Urdu scale, in digits with the scale word: million = 10 «لاکھ», ten million = 1 «کروڑ», a thousand million = 1 «ارب»; thousands as the source («16,000»); a decimal is kept where the conversion leaves one («1.5 لاکھ»). 'More than' is «سے زیادہ» in a sentence. «ملین» and «بلین» are not written. The big figure of the home page takes the compact form, «25 لاکھ+», which is the source's own form; the lead says «25 لاکھ سے زیادہ». Not exercised and not ruled: a sum of money in a foreign currency.
calibration.binds: Every count on every /ur/ page; first the oasis and World Heritage pages (number of palms, area).
calibration.guard: Stage checker (taught after round 1; it reads this entry): where the English or Arabic carries a figure followed by million / M / «مليون», the Urdu carries the same value written with the scale words above — ten times the figure followed by «لاکھ», or a tenth of it followed by «کروڑ» from ten million up; a wrong conversion, a bare converted figure or an unconverted one is a finding. The clauses of the ruling ('million = 10 …', 'ten million = 1 …', 'a thousand million = 1 …', '… and … are not written') are what the tools parse and are to be kept word for word when the ruling is entered in the termbase.
